'''Thomas Burton Loram Kirkwood''' (6 July 1951) is a South-African born English biologist who made his contribution to the biology of ageing by proposing the [[disposable soma theory of aging]]. He is currently a researcher and Associate Dean for Ageing in [[Newcastle University]] and he headed the Institute for Ageing and Health in its school of clinical medical sciences. He is the author of ''Time of Our Lives: The Science of Human Aging'' (1999), ''The End of Age: Why Everything About Aging Is Changing'' (2001), and co-author of ''Chance, Development, and Aging'' (2000, together with [[Caleb Finch|Caleb E. Finch]]).  In 2001 he gave the annual [[Reith Lectures]].<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p00ghvdn The End of Age]</ref>

He also leads the [[Newcastle 85+ Study]] and on the theme of  the continuing growth in human life expectancy he, on 16 March 2017, delivered a lecture entitled "Why and how are we living longer?" to [[Manchester Literary & Philosophical Society ]]  notes of it may be viewed<ref> Manchester Memoirs VOLUME VOLUME 155 2016 - 2017 Memoirs and Proceedings OF THE Manchester Literary & Philosophical Society </ref>

Kirkwood was appointed [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in the 2009 New Year Honours.<ref>{{London Gazette |issue=58929 |date=31 December 2008 |page=7 |supp=y }}</ref> He was elected a [[Fellow of the Academy of Medical Sciences]] in 2001.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Thomas Kirkwood |url=https://acmedsci.ac.uk/fellows/fellows-directory/ordinary-fellows/fellow/Thomas%20Burton%20Loram-Kirkwood-0033z00002qIIXTAA4 |access-date=2026-06-30 |website=The Academy of Medical Sciences |language=en}}</ref>
